issue.standard_remedy: Consolidate tail suppliers into preferred suppliers
issue.summary: 121 of 160 suppliers share the last 20% of category spend

plan.diagnosis: Electric motors category exhibits severe fragmentation with 121 suppliers accounting for only 20% of spend (USD 15,626,622), yielding an HHI of 1023 that signals atomized purchasing and foregone volume leverage. With Meridian Components K.K. holding 29.6% share as top supplier, consolidating the 121 tail suppliers into preferred tier-1 vendors will eliminate redundant supplier relationships and unlock 8-12% tail-spend savings through economies of scale.

remedy_steps.step: Conduct RFx for electric motors with top 5 existing suppliers (including Meridian Components K.K.) to secure volume discounts for absorbing USD 15,626,622 tail spend; target 10% cost reduction and establish preferred supplier agreements with tiered rebates.

Map all 121 tail suppliers' part numbers to preferred supplier equivalents; validate technical specifications, lead times, and certifications; obtain cross-reference matrix from engineering and quality teams.

Implement supplier rationalization: migrate 80% of tail volume (USD 12,501,298) to 3-4 preferred suppliers; issue supplier exit notices to non-strategic vendors; consolidate POs in Coupa and update source lists across SAP, Oracle EBS, Dynamics 365, and NetSuite.

Execute ERP changes: block exited tail suppliers in SAP (LFA1 posting block), Oracle EBS (Supplier Hold), Dynamics 365 and NetSuite (Inactive status); create exclusive source list entries for electric motors commodity codes pointing to preferred suppliers; enforce requisition workflow approvals for any non-preferred sourcing.

Negotiate extended payment terms (Net-60 to Net-90) with preferred suppliers in exchange for volume commitment; establish quarterly business reviews and continuous improvement KPIs; document category strategy playbook.

plan.expected_impact: Consolidating 121 tail suppliers will yield USD 1,562,662 in annual savings (10% of USD 15,626,622 tail spend) through volume leverage, reduced transaction costs, and improved payment terms.
kpis: Tail supplier count reduction from 121 to <30 within 6 months
Electric motors category HHI increase from 1023 to >1800
Tail spend as % of category reduced from 20% to <10%
PO count reduction of >60% in electric motors category
risks: Supply disruption if tail suppliers exit before preferred suppliers ramp volume; mitigate with 90-day transition buffer and safety stock.
Engineering resistance to alternative part numbers; require early cross-functional validation and pilot conversions.
Preferred suppliers may lack capacity for full tail volume absorption; secure capacity commitments in RFx phase.
Multi-ERP environment creates data synchronization delays; assign dedicated ERP admin for parallel system updates.
Incumbent tail suppliers may hold sole-source or proprietary designs; identify and retain strategic niche vendors (estimate 15-20 of 121).
erp_actions: SAP: Set posting block in LFA1/LFB1 for exited tail suppliers; add source list entries (ME01) for electric motors material groups linking to preferred suppliers with validity dates; change payment terms to Net-90 in vendor master (XK02) for preferred suppliers.

Oracle EBS: Apply Supplier Hold at site level for tail suppliers; create Approved Supplier List (ASL) entries for electric motors category restricting to preferred vendors; update payment terms in supplier master.

Dynamics 365: Set supplier status to Inactive for tail vendors; configure Trade Agreements for preferred suppliers with tiered pricing; update Procurement Categories to enforce preferred supplier workflows.
NetSuite: Inactivate tail supplier records; create Item/Vendor relationships for electric motors items restricted to preferred suppliers; set up Vendor Price Lists with volume discounts.

Coupa: Update supplier status to Blocked for tail vendors; configure Preferred Supplier rules in catalog and sourcing workflows; create Supplier Segmentation tags (Preferred/Tactical/Exit) for reporting; enable requisition approval routing for non-preferred electric motor requests.
